title: VerificationStoreRepository
responsibility: Stores verification drafts with their evidence until they are persisted as Git evidence.

inputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.constructor.root
inputs.description: Repository root used to derive the verification scratch-store path under .cache/harness/verifications. The constructor joins this string with that relative directory but does not create or validate the path.

inputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.directoryFor.commit
inputs.description: Commit string used as the commit directory under the verification scratch store. This method passes it to path.join without checking that it is a full commit hash.

inputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.directoryFor.startedAt
inputs.description: Run start timestamp used to form the run directory component. Non-digits are removed and at most the first 17 remaining digits are kept; shorter values remain shorter.

inputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.save.record
inputs.description: Verification record serialized into record.json with tab indentation. The repository does not validate the record before writing it.

inputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.save.directory
inputs.description: Directory in which save creates record.json. It creates the directory recursively and uses the supplied path without requiring it to be inside the scratch store.

inputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.load.reference
inputs.description: A stored record ID or a path to a record file; a resolved existing file is read before any ID search. An invalid file or an unmatched ID returns undefined.

inputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.latest.commit
inputs.description: Commit string used to filter records by record.source.commit. It is compared exactly and is not validated as a SHA by this method.

inputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.read.path
inputs.description: File-system path to one record JSON file. Missing, unreadable, malformed, or schema-invalid content returns undefined.

outputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.directoryFor
outputs.description: Store directory path formed from the repository root, .cache/harness/verifications, the commit string, and the sanitized timestamp. The timestamp component contains at most 17 digits, and this method creates no directories.

outputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.save
outputs.description: A promise that resolves with no value after the directory is recursively created and tab-indented record.json is written with a trailing newline. It does not validate the record, and file-system failures reject the promise.

outputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.load
outputs.description: A valid stored record with its containing directory, or undefined when no valid file or matching record ID is found. Existing file references take precedence over ID lookup.

outputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.latest
outputs.description: The valid stored record for the exact source commit with the greatest startedAt string under descending comparison, regardless of outcome. Returns undefined when no record matches.

outputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.all
outputs.description: An array of all valid stored records in commit/run directory traversal order. Invalid records are skipped, and a missing store produces an empty array.

outputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.records
outputs.description: A lazy iterator that yields valid stored records in commit/run directory traversal order without retaining the full history. If the store directory is absent it yields nothing; directory enumeration failures propagate when consumed.

outputs.name: VerificationStoreRepository.read
outputs.description: A valid record parsed from the file together with its parent directory. Missing, unreadable, malformed, or schema-invalid files return undefined.

errors.name: Verification store filesystem failure
errors.description: Unhandled file-system failures from recursive directory creation, file writing, store traversal, or file stat can throw or reject from the corresponding methods. read catches file-read, JSON-parse, and validation failures and returns undefined; operating-system error codes vary by cause.
